mechanism_narrative: Persistently low WORKPLACES mobility signals a weak weekday activity base, and that suppresses discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks. If commuting demand stays depressed, RETAIL_REC should remain below its last-four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean for four consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays at or below its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from its recent trough increases access to shopping corridors within 1-2 weeks, lifting retail visits shortly after the transit improvement. The effect should show up first as higher RETAIL_REC when transit stops falling and begins to recover.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points week-on-week after being below -40 for two weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain depressed, people substitute local errands and neighborhood shopping for longer trips, which supports retail activity over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when the residential uplift persists alongside weak commuting.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline but RETAIL_REC falls below its prior 4-week mean for the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES remains suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERy_PHARM drops sharply after being near baseline, it indicates a broader tightening in discretionary errand traffic, which should spill over into retail and recreation within one week. A sudden weakening in routine shopping is a leading indicator for lower RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8 after previously staying above -5 for at least 2 weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -8 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained PARKS surge raises outing intensity and can divert leisure time away from enclosed retail venues, producing a short-lived decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if outdoor activity and shopping rise together instead of substituting for each other.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 25 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS stays above 25 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals stronger daytime foot traffic and denser trip chaining, which should translate into higher retail visits over the next four weeks. The signal requires both commuting and workplace activity to improve together.
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise from their current levels but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior dip can precede a retail uptick because more out-of-home leisure activity increases incidental shopping and dining trips within two weeks. This leading effect should appear only when parks mobility is recovering from weakness, not when it is already elevated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 10 points after one week below 20
failure_condition: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from a weak week but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM both rise while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, the city is shifting toward home-centered and necessity-only travel, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its last-four-week average over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when reduced transit access constrains discretionary shopping trips.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM stay elevated while TRANSIT remains below -35, but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean within 4 weeks.
